groups.name: Groundbreaking LGBTQ+ representation on TV
groups.explanation: Orphan Black (featured trans character Tony and clone storylines exploring gender), Transparent (centered on a trans parent coming out), Pose (Black and Latinx LGBTQ+ ballroom culture), and It's a Sin (gay men during the AIDS crisis in 1980s London) were all landmark TV shows celebrated for LGBTQ+ representation at the time they aired.

groups.name: TV characters who idolize or model themselves on a doomed literary or historical outlaw
groups.explanation: Jax Teller (Sons of Anarchy) fashions himself after Hamlet and the romantic outlaw biker archetype; Jamie Fraser (Outlander) identifies with the doomed Jacobite rebel warrior tradition; Nate Archibald (Gossip Girl) repeatedly models himself on classic tragic-romantic literary figures; and Lip Gallagher (Shameless US) is explicitly coded as a self-destructive working-class intellectual in the mold of the doomed gifted outsider — each character consciously or unconsciously channels a romantic outlaw template that ultimately contributes to their downfall.

groups.name: Actors who played the Devil — not a demon, not an angel — specifically Satan on screen
groups.explanation: These four tiles are all connected to portrayals of Satan specifically: 'I know what I am.' is the Devil's signature line from Lucifer; The Pines is the location in Reaper where the Devil (Ray Wise) appears; Tatiana Maslany voiced Satan in the animated show Little Demon; Ian McShane played a version of the Devil in American Gods. Players will be misdirected by Tatiana Maslany toward Orphan Black clones and Ian McShane toward Deadwood's Al Swearengen.

groups.name: TV antagonists whose name is also the name of a DC Comics character
groups.explanation: Flea is a villain alias in The Flash TV universe AND a DC Comics villain; Eugene Tooms (X-Files) shares his name with a minor DC villain; Harvey Dent is famously Two-Face in DC Comics and appears as an antagonist in Gotham; The Upside Down from Stranger Things shares its name with a DC Comics universe/dimension concept. Players will assume these tiles go with horror, sci-fi, or comic book adaptations, missing that the unifying thread is the name overlap with DC Comics characters.
